title: A/B Rebalancing Runbook and Ownership Lattice (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook for cross-functional A/B and canary rebalancing. Primary goal: provide a compact operations playbook that clarifies ownership during traffic shifts, defines the rebalancing lattice (who adjusts what and when), and prescribes teardown criteria. This doc is experimental — intended to be used during pilot rollouts and to collect field notes for a later formal playbook.

Scope and motivations:
- Target audience: product owners, release engineers, solutions eng, SRE oncall, data scientists monitoring evals.
- Why this exists: we repeatedly see mid-rollout manual rebalances that cause oscillation, cost overruns, and unclear incident ownership. The lattice formalizes responsibilities and step-ordering to reduce coordination friction.

Key concepts (terms we use)
- Ownership lattice: a small matrix mapping teams to control levers (traffic, model variant, quality gates, cost throttle) and escalation path.
- Rebalancing window: the time segment where traffic weights are allowed to change (default 30m).
- Variance budget: pre-allocated tolerance for primary metrics (latency, cost per token, negative-sentiment delta) to permit small fluctuation without manual rollback.
- Payoff matrix: quick decision table for when to expand, pause, or roll back based on signal and cost tradeoff.

Runbook quick flow (90s skim)
1) Observe: telemetry triggers (alert or steward request) -> notify steward channel #rollouts.
2) Triage: steward + oncall SRE decide if signal is noise (within variance budget). If noise, note and monitor (document in JIRA).
3) Contain: if outside budget, apply containment action in order of lattice: (a) disable feature-level sampling bake, (b) route to fallback variant, (c) reduce experiment weight by configured step.
4) Investigate: solutions eng and data scientist run rapid evals on sample logs and golden prompts.
5) Remediate: apply targeted fix or rollback; record decision and metric deltas.
6) Teardown: run postmortem checklist, reclaim traffic, and update payoff matrix with observed outcomes.

Ownership lattice (compact)
- Product/PM: hypothesis, acceptance criteria, release window, stakeholder comms.
- Solutions Eng: shepherds experiment runbook, runbook templates, operator handoffs, QA prompts set.
- Release Eng / SRE: executes traffic changes, applies surge/containment knobs, maintains routing infra.
- Data Science / Eval: signal definition, metric calculation, A/B statistical check, drift detection.
- Cost Ops / Finance (optional): approves burst cost limits and monitors spend alarms.

Rebalancing knobs (ordered by recommended use)
1) Micro-step weight shifts: 1–5% per rebalancing window. Use for marginal signal.
2) Cohort isolation: move affected cohorts (geos/accounts) out of experiment.
3) Model variant swap: promote stable variant as fallback.
4) Traffic siphon to canary pool: route a fixed small set to isolated infra for deeper inspection.
5) Full-step rollback: revert to control. Only under confirmed regression.

Playoff/payoff matrix (example)
- Signal: latency increase 10% over baseline, no quality drop, cost +5% -> Action: reduce weight by 10% and monitor 2 windows.
- Signal: quality metric drop (QA prompts > 3 points), latency unchanged -> Action: cohort isolation + model variant swap.
- Signal: cost spike (unexpected >25%) with no clear quality regression -> Action: enable cost-throttle, notify finance, pause expansion.

Signal handling recipes
- Burn-in probe: when enabling a new slice, run a 10min synthetic traffic probe with golden prompts; compare token-per-response distribution.
- Signal enrichment: attach sample payloads to telemetry alert (redact PII) and pin to incident thread.
- Confidence ramp: require 3 consecutive windows in the desired direction before promoting weights.

Teardown checklist (post-run)
- Reclaim weights: roll weights back to baseline allocation or next planned step.
- Snapshot artifacts: save model version, route config, traces, evaluation runs to linkedasses (JIRA).
- Cost reconciliation: capture delta vs expected cost, annotate deviations.
- Update payoff matrix and lattice decisions: what changed? Who acted? Time stamp.
- Lessons & next steps: list 1–3 action items and assign owners.

Operational templates
- Slack headline (steward): [ROLLOUT] {experiment} — observed {signal}. Actions taken: {containment}. Owner: {name}. Next update in 30m.
- Jira quick label: rollout-triage, experiment-{id}, severity-{low|medium|high}.
- Release task checklist: preflight (golden prompts), infra capacity check, variance budget set, rollback playbook attached.

Guardrails and heuristics (field rules)
- Never change routing + model variant in the same window unless in emergency.
- If cost > 50% of reserved committed capacity, pause experiment and escalate to finance lead.
- For cross-region rollouts, prefer region-by-region incrementalization (not global) to reduce blast radius.

Data / telemetry primitives we expect
- Experiment_state: {weight, variant, start_ts, steward} (recorded as a line in release logs).
- Key metrics: p50/p95 latency, cost-per-token, negative-feedback-rate, autoreject-rate, hallucination-regression (score).
- Comparison window: 3x rebalancing windows by default (90m) for stable readouts.

Open questions / things to iterate on
- How to automate variance budget adjustments per experiment class? (low-risk UI vs high-risk safety experiments).
- Should we expose a 'traffic reclaim' API for product teams to reclaim unused slices? Ownership and billing implications.
- Better tooling for sample redaction before attaching to telemetry.

Field notes (live)
- 2025-02-18: small experiment on reranker saw p95 latency bump after third traffic step; manual micro-step rollback avoided rollback — good case for micro-step defaults.
- 2025-02-26: cohort isolation saved a major customer from exposure; need a checklist for customer-owned cohorts.

Next actions (this doc)
- Convert lattice into compact YAML for use in release UI (owner: Sofia Kim, due 2025-03-10).
- Prototype 'variance budget' UI with cost knobs (owner: Jamal Rivera, due 2025-03-17).
- Run a dry-run rehearsal with SRE and Solutions Eng next sprint (owner: Priya Nambiar).

Appendix: quick decision heuristics (for oncall)
- If metric falls within +/- variance budget -> monitor only.
- If metric outside variance budget and impacts >1 cohort -> contain (isolate cohorts) then escalate.
- If cost spike without quality impact -> apply cost-throttle before rollback.

References and links:
- Confluence: rollout-ops playbook (see linked artifact CONFLUENCE-ROLL-789)
- JIRA: incident and experiment tracking prefix JIRA-RST-2145
- Repo: rollout-scripts PR 423 for traffic-siphon helper

Notes to self: keep the lattice intentionally small. The more knobs we add the slower decisions become. Capture one exemplar after each pilot and iterate.
